tasks.context: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What message does the woman convey in her book?

options.A: Prioritizing happiness over money.
options.B: Joining the club to get her new book.
options.C: Managing one's personal finances wisely.
options.D: Consuming more only when earning

questions.cn: 女士在她的书里传达了什么信息？

optionsCn.A: 把幸福置于金钱之上。
optionsCn.B: 加入俱乐部以获取她的新书。
optionsCn.C: 明智地管理个人财务。
optionsCn.D: 只在挣得多时才多消费。

questions.stem: What do we learn about the woman before she became a writer?

options.A: She was in debt.
options.B: She was a financial adviser.
options.C: She earned $ 30,000 a month.
options.D: She enjoyed a happy life.

questions.cn: 关于成为作家之前的女士，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 她负债。
optionsCn.B: 她是理财顾问。
optionsCn.C: 她每月挣 3 万美元。
optionsCn.D: 她过着幸福的生活。

questions.stem: What does the woman say about one's financial behavior?

options.A: It reflects one's earning power.
options.B: It varies with one's environment.
options.C: It mirrors one's sense of wellbeing.
options.D: It changes with one's goals in life.

questions.cn: 关于一个人的理财行为，女士说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它反映一个人的挣钱能力。
optionsCn.B: 它随一个人的环境而变化。
optionsCn.C: 它映照一个人的幸福感。
optionsCn.D: 它随人生目标的变化而变化。

questions.stem: What does the man say about sharing a home?

options.A: It would give him more time to be with his loved ones.
options.B: It would be good for those who value relationships.
options.C: It would mean major sacrifices for him.
options.D: It would deprive him of his individuality.

questions.cn: 关于合住，男士说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 这会让他有更多时间与所爱之人相处。
optionsCn.B: 这对看重人际关系的人是好事。
optionsCn.C: 对他来说这意味着很大的牺牲。
optionsCn.D: 这会剥夺他的个性。

lines.t: Conversation 1.
lines.cn: 对话一。

lines.t: M: Welcome to the Book Club.
lines.cn: M：欢迎来到《读书俱乐部》。

lines.t: M: Today's guest is Susan Lane, the author of a new book on personal finances that has already sold half a million copies.
lines.cn: M：今天的嘉宾是苏珊·莱恩，她一本关于个人理财的新书已经卖出了五十万册。

lines.t: M: Hi, Susan.
lines.cn: M：你好，苏珊。

lines.t: M: Your book is extremely successful.
lines.cn: M：你的书非常成功。

lines.t: M: Why do you think that is?
lines.cn: M：你觉得这是为什么？

lines.t: F: I think that's because of my message, which is making happiness a priority over money.
lines.cn: F：我想是因为我传达的信息：把幸福置于金钱之上。

lines.t: F: So many of us in my generation have spent decades trying to earn more money just to consume more, but it made us more miserable.
lines.cn: F：我们这一代很多人花了几十年努力挣更多的钱，只是为了消费更多，结果却更痛苦。

lines.t: M: You yourself were once caught in that cycle, working for two decades as an executive and earning a high salary, but still accumulating debt.
lines.cn: M：你自己也曾陷入那种循环，做了二十年高管、拿着高薪，却还在不断积累债务。

lines.t: F: I most certainly was.
lines.cn: F：确实如此。

lines.t: F: I earned millions, but by the time I quit my job four years ago to become a writer, I owed over $30,000.
lines.cn: F：我挣过几百万，但四年前辞职去当作家时，我欠了三万多美元。

lines.t: M: So how did you escape that pattern, and what would you advise other people to do?
lines.cn: M：那你是怎么摆脱那种模式的？你会建议别人怎么做？

lines.t: F: The first change is in what we value.
lines.cn: F：第一个改变在于我们看重什么。

lines.t: F: We need to emphasize things that actually make us happy, like relationships, the environment, or even our hobbies.
lines.cn: F：我们需要重视那些真正让我们幸福的东西，比如人际关系、环境，甚至我们的爱好。

lines.t: F: Once we make the right things our priority, our goals will change, and so will our financial behavior.
lines.cn: F：一旦我们把对的东西放在优先位置，我们的目标就会改变，我们的理财行为也会改变。

lines.t: M: How does that translate into practical action?
lines.cn: M：这如何转化为实际行动？

lines.t: M: Can you give our audience examples of what you're talking about on an everyday basis?
lines.cn: M：你能给我们的听众举些日常生活中的例子吗？

lines.t: F: The major areas for action are usually housing, food, and transportation.
lines.cn: F：主要的行动领域通常是住房、饮食和交通。

lines.t: F: So, people might share a home with friends instead of living on their own, bring lunch from home instead of going to restaurants, and use public transport instead of owning a car.
lines.cn: F：比如，人们可以和朋友们合住而不是独居，从家里带午饭而不是去餐馆，用公共交通而不是自己买车。

lines.t: M: Those sound like major sacrifices.
lines.cn: M：这些听起来是很大的牺牲。

lines.t: M: I could never share my home.
lines.cn: M：我可做不到和别人合住。

lines.t: M: I need my own space.
lines.cn: M：我需要自己的空间。

lines.t: F: But they aren't sacrifices.
lines.cn: F：但它们不是牺牲。

lines.t: F: When people change their values, their desires change.
lines.cn: F：当人们改变价值观时，他们的欲望也会改变。

lines.t: F: So in the example of housing, if we value relationships, sharing a home isn't depriving ourselves of space, but giving us an opportunity to spend more time with our loved ones.
lines.cn: F：就拿住房来说，如果我们看重人际关系，合住就不是剥夺自己的空间，而是给我们一个与所爱之人多相处一会儿的机会。

lines.t: M: Indeed it is.
lines.cn: M：确实如此。

tasks.title: Sec A · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do we learn about one of the newest additions to the Gallery's collection?

options.A: It was the artist's first landscape.
options.B: It was a painting by Christopher.
options.C: It was donated by the artist herself.
options.D: It was displayed at a retirement party.

questions.cn: 关于画廊藏品中最新的一件，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 那是这位艺术家的第一幅风景画。
optionsCn.B: 那是克里斯托弗画的一幅画。
optionsCn.C: 那是艺术家本人捐赠的。
optionsCn.D: 它曾在一场退休欢送会上展出。

questions.stem: What does the man say about one of the most acclaimed paintings by Daniel Gregory?

options.A: It was the painting that instantly made her rich.
options.B: It has cost him a lot of money to purchase it.
options.C: It was recently purchased by the gallery.
options.D: It is owned by an anonymous collector.

questions.cn: 关于丹妮尔·格雷戈里最受赞誉的画作之一，男士说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 正是这幅画让她一夜暴富。
optionsCn.B: 他花了很多钱才买下它。
optionsCn.C: 画廊最近买下了它。
optionsCn.D: 它属于一位匿名收藏家。

questions.stem: Why does the woman say she can feel immersed in the scene in the painting?

options.A: It reflects her emotions.
options.B: It contains ample details.
options.C: It appears perfectly symmetrical.
options.D: It depicts the beauty of desolation.

questions.cn: 女士为什么说她能感到自己沉浸在画中的场景里？

optionsCn.A: 它反映了她的情绪。
optionsCn.B: 它包含丰富的细节。
optionsCn.C: 它看起来完全对称。
optionsCn.D: 它描绘了荒凉之美。

questions.stem: How does the man describe Daniel Gregory?

options.A: She is eccentric like any other artist.
options.B: She is a very nice and intelligent artist.
options.C: She is as lucky as any acclaimed artist.
options.D: She is one of the most productive artists.

questions.cn: 男士如何描述丹妮尔·格雷戈里？

optionsCn.A: 她像其他艺术家一样古怪。
optionsCn.B: 她是一位非常友善且聪慧的艺术家。
optionsCn.C: 她和任何受赞誉的艺术家一样幸运。
optionsCn.D: 她是最多产的艺术家之一。

lines.t: Conversation 2.
lines.cn: 对话二。

lines.t: F: Thank you for inviting me to the gallery, Christopher.
lines.cn: F：克里斯托弗，谢谢你邀请我来画廊。

lines.t: F: I haven't visited here since your predecessor's retirement function.
lines.cn: F：自从你前任的退休欢送会之后，我就没来过这里。

lines.t: M: Would you like to see the newest additions to our collection first, Catherine?
lines.cn: M：凯瑟琳，你想先看看我们收藏里最新的几件藏品吗？

lines.t: F: Are those the landscapes by Danielle Gregory?
lines.cn: F：是丹妮尔·格雷戈里画的那几幅风景画吗？

lines.t: F: I absolutely adore her work.
lines.cn: F：我特别欣赏她的作品。

lines.t: M: This first piece was a gift to the gallery from the artist herself, and it's quite exquisite.
lines.cn: M：这第一幅是艺术家本人送给画廊的礼物，非常精美。

lines.t: F: I love how she depicts the barren landscape.
lines.cn: F：我很喜欢她描绘这片荒芜景色的方式。

lines.t: F: The colors complement each other perfectly.
lines.cn: F：色彩彼此映衬得恰到好处。

lines.t: F: You can sense the desolation in the picture.
lines.cn: F：你能在画中感受到那种荒凉。

lines.t: M: This piece was inspired by Gregory's recent trek in the Gobi Desert.
lines.cn: M：这幅作品的灵感来自格雷戈里最近在戈壁沙漠的徒步旅行。

lines.t: F: And how did you obtain her other piece over here?
lines.cn: F：那这边她另一幅作品你们是怎么得到的？

lines.t: M: It was purchased at auction by an anonymous collector, who lent it to the gallery for display.
lines.cn: M：它由一位匿名收藏家在拍卖会上买下，又借给画廊展出。

lines.t: M: This composition is one of her most acclaimed paintings.
lines.cn: M：这幅构图是她最受赞誉的画作之一。

lines.t: F: It must have cost that collector a small fortune to purchase this.
lines.cn: F：那位收藏家买下它一定花了一大笔钱。

lines.t: M: Obviously.
lines.cn: M：显然是的。

lines.t: M: I can't disclose the exact amount he paid, but it was substantial.
lines.cn: M：我不能透露他具体付了多少钱，但那数目相当可观。

lines.t: F: There's so much detail in this painting.
lines.cn: F：这幅画里细节太多了。

lines.t: F: I feel like I can really immerse myself in the scene.
lines.cn: F：我感觉自己真的能沉浸在这个场景里。

lines.t: F: I particularly like the symmetry created by the reflection of the mountain in the lake.
lines.cn: F：我特别喜欢山峦在湖中倒影所形成的对称。

lines.t: M: This particular piece was the one that was nominated for a Gateway Award.
lines.cn: M：正是这一幅获得了“门户奖”提名。

lines.t: M: I was lucky enough to attend the award ceremony as Gregory's guest.
lines.cn: M：我有幸作为格雷戈里的嘉宾出席了颁奖典礼。

lines.t: F: So, you know her personally.
lines.cn: F：这么说，你私下认识她。

lines.t: F: I assume she's an eccentric artist.
lines.cn: F：我猜她是个古怪的艺术家。

lines.t: M: Quite the opposite, in fact.
lines.cn: M：其实恰恰相反。

lines.t: M: She's not at all eccentric.
lines.cn: M：她一点也不古怪。

lines.t: M: I would say she's one of the most easygoing and intelligent people I know.
lines.cn: M：要我说，她是我认识的最随和、最聪明的人之一。

lines.t: F: I'd love to be able to meet her.
lines.cn: F：我很想能见见她。

lines.t: F: There are so many questions I'd like to ask.
lines.cn: F：我有太多问题想问。

lines.t: M: What a coincidence.
lines.cn: M：真巧。

lines.t: M: I'm meeting her for dinner tonight.
lines.cn: M：我今晚就和她一起吃晚饭。

lines.t: M: Would you like to come along?
lines.cn: M：你想一起来吗？

lines.t: F: I'd love to.
lines.cn: F：我很愿意。

lines.t: F: Thank you.
lines.cn: F：谢谢。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the passage say about forgiveness?

options.A: It is vital to one's mental health.
options.B: It leads to reconciliation and peace.
options.C: It promotes interpersonal relationship.
options.D: It keeps one from traumatic experience.

questions.cn: 关于宽恕，文章说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它对一个人的心理健康至关重要。
optionsCn.B: 它带来和解与平静。
optionsCn.C: 它促进人际关系。
optionsCn.D: 它使人免于创伤经历。

questions.stem: When is forgiveness especially challenging?

options.A: When the offender has power over the victim.
options.B: When the offender is not willing to apologize.
options.C: When the offender is not duly penalized
options.D: When the offender adds insult to injury.

questions.cn: 什么时候宽恕尤其困难？

optionsCn.A: 当伤害者对受害者有权势时。
optionsCn.B: 当伤害者不愿道歉时。
optionsCn.C: 当伤害者没有被恰当处罚时。
optionsCn.D: 当伤害者雪上加霜时。

questions.stem: What should one do in order to forgive the offender?

options.A: Talk with the offender calmly.
options.B: Accept the offender's apology.
options.C: Find out why he committed the offense.
options.D: Determine how serious the offense was.

questions.cn: 为了宽恕伤害者，一个人应该怎么做？

optionsCn.A: 冷静地与伤害者交谈。
optionsCn.B: 接受伤害者的道歉。
optionsCn.C: 弄清楚他为什么这么做。
optionsCn.D: 判断这一冒犯有多严重。

lines.t: Passage 1.
lines.cn: 短文一。

lines.t: Forgiveness is the release of resentment or anger.
lines.cn: 宽恕是放下怨恨或愤怒。

lines.t: Forgiveness doesn't mean reconciliation.
lines.cn: 宽恕并不意味着和解。

lines.t: We don't have to return to the same relationship, nor do we have to accept the same harmful behaviors from an offender.
lines.cn: 我们不必回到原来的关系，也不必接受伤害者同样的有害行为。

lines.t: Forgiveness is vitally important for the mental health of certain victims.
lines.cn: 对某些受害者来说，宽恕对心理健康至关重要。

lines.t: It propels people forward rather than keeping them emotionally engaged in an injustice or trauma.
lines.cn: 它推动人向前走，而不是让他们在情感上一直困在一段不公或创伤之中。

lines.t: Carrying the hurt or anger of an offense leads the body to release stress chemicals.
lines.cn: 背负着伤害或愤怒，会促使身体释放压力化学物质。

lines.t: Eliminating the perpetual flow of those chemicals may also explain why forgiveness provides physical health benefits.
lines.cn: 消除这些化学物质的持续分泌，或许也能解释宽恕为何对身体健康有益。

lines.t: There are scenarios in which forgiveness is not the best course.
lines.cn: 有些情形下，宽恕并不是最好的做法。

lines.t: Sometimes a victim becomes more empowered when they give themselves permission not to forgive.
lines.cn: 有时，当受害者允许自己不去宽恕时，反而会更有力量。

lines.t: Forgiveness can be challenging.
lines.cn: 宽恕可能很难。

lines.t: This is especially true when the offending party offers an insincere apology, or maybe they haven't offered anything at all.
lines.cn: 当伤害方给出虚假的道歉，或者根本什么都没表示时，尤其如此。

lines.t: However, it's often the healthiest path forward.
lines.cn: 然而，它往往是向前走最健康的一条路。

lines.t: It's important to cultivate forgiveness by developing compassion for the offender.
lines.cn: 通过培养对伤害者的同情心来修炼宽恕很重要。

lines.t: Reflect on whether the act was due to malicious intent, or whether it was caused by challenging circumstances in the offender's life.
lines.cn: 想一想这个行为是出于恶意，还是由伤害者生活中艰难的处境造成的。

lines.t: What about forgiving ourselves?
lines.cn: 那宽恕自己呢？

lines.t: We sometimes need to take responsibility for mistakes, but intense guilt and shame aren't a desirable outcome in the long run.
lines.cn: 我们有时需要为错误承担责任，但从长远看，强烈的内疚和羞耻并不是理想的结果。

lines.t: Forgiving yourself may seem like an ambiguous process.
lines.cn: 宽恕自己似乎是一个含糊不清的过程。

lines.t: You can begin by acknowledging that you are at fault.
lines.cn: 你可以从承认自己有错开始。

lines.t: Take responsibility for the hurt you caused.
lines.cn: 为自己造成的伤害承担责任。

lines.t: Then, reflect on why the event occurred.
lines.cn: 然后，想一想这件事为什么会发生。

lines.t: Draw the lessons you learned and try to avoid committing a similar offense in the future.
lines.cn: 吸取你得到的教训，并努力避免将来再犯类似的错误。

questions.stem: What does the passage say about the Glasgow subway in the 1960s?

options.A: The number of passengers dropped sharply.
options.B: It served more and more commuters.
options.C: The number of stations increased to 50.
options.D: It became the longest in the United Kingdom.

questions.cn: 关于 20 世纪 60 年代的格拉斯哥地铁，文章说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 乘客数量急剧下降。
optionsCn.B: 它服务的通勤者越来越多。
optionsCn.C: 车站数量增加到了 50 个。
optionsCn.D: 它成为英国最长的地铁。

questions.stem: Why was the Glasgow subway closed in 1977?

options.A: To increase capacity to meet growing needs.
options.B: To make way for other means of transport.
options.C: To have its systems modernised.
options.D: To avoid further financial losses.

optionsCn.A: 为满足不断增长的需求而提高运力。
optionsCn.B: 为其他交通方式让路。
optionsCn.C: 对其系统进行现代化改造。
optionsCn.D: 避免进一步的财务损失。

questions.stem: Why does the Glasgow subway remain important today?

options.A: It is generally recognised as a world heritage site.
options.B: It is the fastest way to reach the city's south side.
options.C: It constitutes a source of revenue for the city.
options.D: It helps reduce traffic jams in the city centre.

questions.cn: 格拉斯哥地铁为何至今仍重要？

optionsCn.A: 它普遍被认定为世界遗产。
optionsCn.B: 它是抵达城市南侧最快的方式。
optionsCn.C: 它为这座城市带来财政收入。
optionsCn.D: 它有助于缓解市中心的交通拥堵。

questions.stem: What does the passage say about all subway stations in Glasgow nowadays? From the four choices, mark A, B, C, and D.

options.A: They are usually crowded.
options.B: They use high-tech systems.
options.C: They accept smartcards only.
options.D: They are colourfully decorated.

questions.cn: 关于如今年格拉斯哥的所有地铁站，文章说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它们通常很拥挤。
optionsCn.B: 它们使用高科技系统。
optionsCn.C: 它们只接受智能卡。
optionsCn.D: 它们装饰得色彩缤纷。

lines.t: Passage 2.
lines.cn: 短文二。

lines.t: The Glasgow Subway first opened in 1896 as a cable-hauled system.
lines.cn: 格拉斯哥地铁最初于 1896 年开通，是一套缆索牵引系统。

lines.t: It is generally recognized as the world's third underground railway, after London and Budapest.
lines.cn: 它通常被认为是世界上第三条地下铁路，仅次于伦敦和布达佩斯。

lines.t: In its long history, it has never been expanded, remaining as a single loop line with a mere 15 stations.
lines.cn: 在漫长的历史中，它从未扩建，始终是一条仅有 15 个车站的单一环线。

lines.t: At its peak, it served the shipyard workers on the south side of the city.
lines.cn: 在鼎盛时期，它服务于城市南侧的船厂工人。

lines.t: In the 1960s, there was a decline in the shipbuilding industry, and the popularity of private transport grew.
lines.cn: 20 世纪 60 年代，造船业衰落，私人交通工具日益普及。

lines.t: As a result, the subway saw a rapid decline in ridership.
lines.cn: 结果，地铁乘客量迅速下降。

lines.t: It ran with little further change until 1977, when its new operators closed it for major modernization investment.
lines.cn: 此后它几乎没有什么变化地运行到 1977 年，新运营商为进行大规模现代化投资而将其关闭。

lines.t: Carriages were replaced, ventilation was improved, and the main depot was also renovated and fitted with connecting tracks to replace the outdated crane transfer mechanism.
lines.cn: 车厢被更换，通风得到改善，主车库也进行了翻修，并加装了连接轨道以取代过时的吊车转运装置。

lines.t: The subway in its present form reopened for operation in April 1980.
lines.cn: 现代形态的地铁于 1980 年 4 月重新开通运营。

lines.t: Since its relaunch, the subway has seen a revival in its fortunes.
lines.cn: 自重新开通以来，地铁的命运得以复苏。

lines.t: It serves as a viable alternative to other forms of transport and has gone a long way to alleviate traffic jams in the city centre.
lines.cn: 它成为其他交通方式之外一个可行的选择，并在很大程度上缓解了市中心的交通拥堵。

lines.t: In 1996, the system reached an important milestone, 100 years.
lines.cn: 1996 年，该系统迎来了一个重要里程碑——100 年。

lines.t: To commemorate this special event, the colour scheme of the train carriages was updated.
lines.cn: 为纪念这一特别事件，列车车厢的配色方案也做了更新。

lines.t: Recently, high-tech systems such as smart card ticketing machines and smart gates are used across all subway stations.
lines.cn: 最近，智能卡售票机和智能闸机等高科技系统已在所有地铁站使用。

lines.t: The smart card provides more convenient travel, and passengers simply top up their cards and tap them to get in and out the subway.
lines.cn: 智能卡让出行更便捷，乘客只需充值并刷卡进出地铁。

lines.t: Since its launch, the technology has been adopted by more than 100,000 subway customers.
lines.cn: 自推出以来，这项技术已被超过 10 万名地铁乘客采用。

lines.t: Recording 1.
lines.cn: 录音一。

lines.t: If you visit the Great Smoky Mountains National Park, chances are you will remember the roadside or campground bears above all else.
lines.cn: 如果你去大烟山国家公园，你很可能最记得路旁或营地的熊。

lines.t: Bears are the most popular animals in a number of our national parks.
lines.cn: 在我们若干国家公园里，熊都是最受欢迎的动物。

lines.t: In these mountains, where the population of bears runs into the hundreds, opportunities to observe these large wild animals are plentiful during the summer.
lines.cn: 在这些山里，熊的数量可达数百只，夏季观察这些大型野生动物的机会很多。

lines.t: Since national parks are wildlife sanctuaries where no disturbance of the native animals is allowed, years of protection have served to break down the wild bears' fear of humans.
lines.cn: 由于国家公园是野生动植物保护区，不允许干扰本地动物，多年的保护削弱了野熊对人类的恐惧。

lines.t: Now, instead of depending on their own resources for a living, many bears patrol park roads and campgrounds.
lines.cn: 如今，许多熊不再依靠自己的本领谋生，而是在公园道路和营地巡游。

lines.t: They give the garbage cans a frequent going-over.
lines.cn: 它们频繁翻找垃圾桶。

lines.t: An occasional offer of food from a park visitor, an illegal and dangerous practice, makes beggars of them.
lines.cn: 游客偶尔投喂食物——一种非法而危险的做法——让它们变成了乞丐。

lines.t: Bears are very often hungry, and since they will feed on almost any kind of plant or animal, garbage is quite acceptable.
lines.cn: 熊常常很饿，而且几乎什么植物或动物都吃，所以垃圾对它们完全可接受。

lines.t: Feeding them, however, represents misguided kindness because the bears come to expect such generosity from everyone and, consequently, trouble could lie ahead.
lines.cn: 然而投喂它们是一种误导的善意，因为熊会开始指望人人都这么慷慨，因而麻烦可能随之而来。

lines.t: Park rules prohibit the feeding of bears.
lines.cn: 公园规定禁止投喂熊。

lines.t: Violators are arrested.
lines.cn: 违规者会被逮捕。

lines.t: Every year, doctors who have offices near the park treat a number of cases of bear bites and bear scratches.
lines.cn: 每年，在公园附近开诊所的医生都会治疗若干起被熊咬伤、抓伤的病例。

lines.t: Some of the accidents have come about in strange ways.
lines.cn: 有些事故的起因很是离奇。

lines.t: One man was in the process of feeding two small cubs when the mother bear appeared and insisted upon having some of the food.
lines.cn: 一名男子正在喂两只幼熊，母熊出现了，坚持要吃一些食物。

lines.t: Shoving the big bear aside with one hand, the man continued feeding the cubs when suddenly he was struck a fierce blow in the face.
lines.cn: 这名男子一只手把大熊推开，继续喂幼熊，突然脸上挨了狠狠一击。

lines.t: A bear, prompted by the food that a lady kept offering to him, entered the car where the generous person was sitting.
lines.cn: 一只熊被一位女士不断投喂的食物所引诱，钻进了这位慷慨者所坐的车里。

lines.t: Her efforts to push the bear out of the car resulted in injuries.
lines.cn: 她试图把熊推出车外，结果受了伤。

lines.t: A man required medical attention after he applied a lighted cigarette to a bear's nose.
lines.cn: 一名男子把点燃的香烟按在熊的鼻子上，之后需要就医。

lines.t: Another man tried to boost a bear into the front seat of his car so that he might take a picture of a bear sitting beside his wife who was behind the wheel.
lines.cn: 另一名男子试图把一只熊抱进汽车前排座位，想拍一张熊坐在副驾（妻子在驾驶位上）旁边的照片。

lines.t: Because bears prefer roads and campgrounds, the possibility of a hiker meeting up with a bear along park trails is small.
lines.cn: 由于熊更喜欢道路和营地，徒步者在公园小径上遇到熊的可能性很小。

lines.t: But there's always that chance, for a bear seems to know if you are carrying a lunch or a candy bar.
lines.cn: 但机会总是有的，因为熊似乎知道你带着午餐或糖果棒。

lines.t: He may even insist on taking it.
lines.cn: 它甚至可能坚持要拿走。

questions.cn: 关于偏见，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它指的是激进且普遍的看法。

optionsCn.B: 它们使某些职业无法兴旺。

lines.t: Recording 2.
lines.cn: 录音二。

lines.t: Why do we form opinions or attitudes about someone or something without really knowing much about them?
lines.cn: 为什么我们在对某人或某事了解不多的情况下就形成看法或态度？

lines.t: Just hearing something good or bad about a person, a place or thing can influence our opinions positively or negatively.
lines.cn: 仅仅听到关于某人、某地或某事的正面或负面消息，就能正面或负面地影响我们的看法。

lines.t: But letting the opinions of another person determine what our opinions will be is dangerous.
lines.cn: 但让别人的看法决定我们的看法是危险的。

lines.t: Forming opinions about someone or something before really knowing them well is called prejudice.
lines.cn: 在真正了解某人或某事之前就形成看法，叫做偏见。

lines.t: Pre- means before and judice refers to judgment.
lines.cn: “Pre-”意为“之前”，“judice”指判断。

lines.t: Hence, prejudice means to judge before having adequate knowledge.
lines.cn: 因此，偏见意味着在掌握充分知识之前就做出判断。

lines.t: We can be prejudiced toward or against someone or something.
lines.cn: 我们可能对某人或某事有偏袒或偏恶。

lines.t: In either case, we are only allowing ourselves to see half of the picture.
lines.cn: 无论哪种情况，我们都只让自己看到了一半的图景。

lines.t: Very few people or things in this world are all good or all bad.
lines.cn: 这世上极少有人或事是全好或全坏的。

lines.t: Prejudiced attitudes are usually based on myths, half-truths, or incorrect information, and they are dangerous because they can keep us from learning the truth about someone or something.
lines.cn: 偏见性态度通常基于迷思、半真半假的说法或错误信息，它们之所以危险，是因为会妨碍我们了解某人或某事的真相。

lines.t: People form prejudices against others for many reasons.
lines.cn: 人们出于许多原因对他人形成偏见。

lines.t: Differences in their race, religion, gender, or occupation.
lines.cn: 比如种族、宗教、性别或职业的差异。

lines.t: Prejudices keep people apart.
lines.cn: 偏见使人彼此隔离。

lines.t: They keep us from really knowing and understanding each other.
lines.cn: 它使我们无法真正认识和理解彼此。

lines.t: We should feel proud of who we are and the group of people we represent.
lines.cn: 我们应当为自己是谁、自己代表的群体感到自豪。

lines.t: If feelings of pride begin to turn to feelings of superiority when we think that our group or our beliefs are better than those around us, however, then we begin to develop prejudiced attitudes that can be harmful.
lines.cn: 然而，当我们认为自己的群体或信念优于周围人时，自豪感若开始变成优越感，我们就开始产生可能有害的偏见性态度。

lines.t: For example, the prejudiced attitudes of one group may keep another group from attending certain schools, from living in any neighborhood they want, or from getting a job or a promotion.
lines.cn: 例如，一个群体的偏见性态度可能使另一个群体无法进入某些学校、无法住在想住的社区，或无法获得工作或晋升。

lines.t: Extreme feelings of prejudice have caused the deaths of innocent people.
lines.cn: 极端的偏见情绪已造成无辜者的死亡。

lines.t: We are responsible for our own thoughts and opinions.
lines.cn: 我们要为自己的想法和看法负责。

lines.t: When we let someone else tell us what to think about someone or something, we are giving up some control of our own lives.
lines.cn: 当我们让别人告诉我们该如何看待某人或某事时，我们就放弃了一部分对自己生活的掌控。

lines.t: Before you form an attitude or opinion, find out for yourself about the person or the thing in question.
lines.cn: 在你形成态度或看法之前，自己去了解相关的人或事。

lines.t: Sometimes we don't realize that we hold prejudiced attitudes toward or against someone or something.
lines.cn: 有时我们并未意识到自己对某人或某事抱有偏见。

lines.t: We need to carefully examine our lives and our fears, and to ask ourselves whether our attitudes come from our personal knowledge and experience or from rumors and fear of the unknown.
lines.cn: 我们需要认真审视自己的生活和恐惧，问自己：我们的态度是来自个人的知识和经验，还是来自传言和对未知的恐惧。

lines.t: The good news about prejudice is that we are not born with it.
lines.cn: 关于偏见的好消息是：我们并非生来就有偏见。

lines.t: Prejudiced attitudes and opinions develop over time.
lines.cn: 偏见性态度和看法是随时间形成的。

lines.t: But with education and knowledge, we can replace our prejudices with cooperation and understanding.
lines.cn: 但通过教育和知识，我们可以用合作与理解取代偏见。

lines.t: Recording 3.
lines.cn: 录音三。

lines.t: When I started high school, it was a shock.
lines.cn: 我上高中时，那是个冲击。

lines.t: I had spent 8 years fighting my way to be the most popular kid in the Catholic school student body.
lines.cn: 我花了 8 年一路打拼，成了天主教学校学生中最受欢迎的孩子。

lines.t: I had been a big, tough 8th grader, and suddenly I was a lowly 9th grader bullied by the big, tough 12th grade seniors who ran the high school.
lines.cn: 我曾是八年级高大强悍的学生，突然之间成了被高中里那些高大强悍的十二年级学长欺负的、卑微的九年级新生。

lines.t: I realized then that it's nice to strive for something, but that you also have to enjoy the moment you're in and be happy where you are.
lines.cn: 那时我意识到，追求某样东西固然很好，但你也得享受当下的时刻，满足于自己所处的位置。

lines.t: Rock and roll had always been an important part of my life.
lines.cn: 摇滚乐一直是我生活的重要部分。

lines.t: I remember my friends and I used to drive around until the late hours of the nights listening to the music of rock and roll legends.
lines.cn: 我记得我和朋友们常常开着车一直转悠到深夜，听着摇滚传奇们的音乐。

lines.t: During those teenage years, I built friendships that I thought would last a lifetime.
lines.cn: 在那些少年岁月里，我建立了以为会持续一生的友谊。

lines.t: Most people that age think the same thing, but people drift apart.
lines.cn: 大多数那个年纪的人都这么想，但人们终究会渐行渐远。

lines.t: Jobs, families, and tragedies separate people from those lasting friendships.
lines.cn: 工作、家庭和变故把人从那些持久的友谊中分开。

lines.t: The tragedy that separated me from my friends forever was the Vietnam War.
lines.cn: 把我和朋友们永远分开的那场变故，是越南战争。

lines.t: A year after I graduated from high school, I left for Vietnam.
lines.cn: 高中毕业一年后，我去了越南。

lines.t: I came back burned out and tired, as though I had lived 10 lifetimes in the short span of 14 months.
lines.cn: 我回来时身心俱疲，仿佛在短短 14 个月里活过了十辈子。

lines.t: The 14 months I was in the war, I couldn't relate to the friends I had had in high school.
lines.cn: 在战场的 14 个月后，我无法与高中时的朋友们产生共鸣。

lines.t: They still seemed childish, concerned with childish things that weren't important to me.
lines.cn: 他们看起来依然幼稚，关心着对我并不重要的幼稚事情。

lines.t: I was still trying to cope with the death, destruction, and evil I had seen in Vietnam.
lines.cn: 我还在努力应对在越南所见的死亡、毁灭与邪恶。

lines.t: I felt like we had done terrible things to innocent people there, and in turn, I had seen terrible things done to my friends.
lines.cn: 我觉得我们在那里对无辜的人做了可怕的事，而我也看到朋友们遭受了可怕的事。

lines.t: I withdrew from my friends and started college.
lines.cn: 我从朋友中抽身，开始上大学。

lines.t: Then I quit college and took many different jobs.
lines.cn: 然后我退了学，做过许多不同的工作。

lines.t: I spent a lot of my time and money on alcohol and other drugs.
lines.cn: 我把大量时间和金钱花在酒精和其他毒品上。

lines.t: Finally, in an effort to get my life going in the right direction again, I sold everything and took what little money I had and bought myself an airplane ticket to Israel.
lines.cn: 最后，为了让生活重新走上正轨，我卖掉了一切，拿出仅有的一点钱，给自己买了一张去以色列的机票。

lines.t: I went there to study history.
lines.cn: 我去那里学历史。

lines.t: While studying at Haifa University, I met my wife, who was also an American student.
lines.cn: 在海法大学读书时，我遇到了我的妻子，她也是美国学生。

lines.t: I now teach in a high school back in America.
lines.cn: 如今我在美国的一所高中教书。

lines.t: I look at my students and see them struggling with many of the very things I struggled with many years ago.
lines.cn: 看着我的学生，我看到他们正在为许多我多年前也曾挣扎过的事情而苦恼。

lines.t: As a teacher, I try to help them over the rough spots as best I can.
lines.cn: 作为老师，我尽力帮他们渡过那些难关。
